name: Compression With Narrative Payoff

CRITERION: Compression With Narrative Payoff
DESCRIPTION: Score high when a short or highly selective story efficiently establishes context, character, movement, and payoff; score low when brevity produces a sketch or when length adds little usable information.

name: Revision depth: continuity, economy, and closed setups
frozen_block:
CRITERION: Revision depth: continuity, economy, and closed setups
DESCRIPTION: Read the writing prompt and the story, then judge how much substantive reworking the text shows in its CONTENT. Assess four things:
(a) Continuity -- do established facts hold? Character names, ages, relationships, physical details, locations, the timeline, and who knows what at each point should stay consistent, with no drift or contradiction.
(b) Economy -- is each paragraph doing work? Look for redundant sentences, beats restated in different words, throat-clearing before the story starts, and passages that could be cut with no loss.
(c) Closure of setups -- are objects, details, and promises introduced early actually used, paid off, or deliberately left open, rather than simply dropped and forgotten?
(d) Control of tense and point of view -- is the narrating stance held deliberately, with any shift reading as a choice, rather than as the writer losing track mid-scene?
HIGH = the story reads as if it has been gone over: nothing contradicts itself, little could be cut, what is planted is used, the narrating stance is under control.
LOW = the story reads as a single unrevised pass: internal details drift or contradict, passages repeat or wander, elements are introduced and abandoned, the narrating stance slips without purpose.
EXPLICITLY IGNORE all spelling, punctuation, capitalization, apostrophes, paragraph spacing, and formatting. A story riddled with typos can and should score HIGH here if the four properties above hold; a mechanically flawless story can and should score LOW if they do not. Do not reward ambition, subject matter, genre, length, or prose flourish; judge only (a)-(d). Use only the prompt and the story -- do not speculate about the writer, and do not consider how the story was received.

name: Earned idea payoff from the premise
frozen_block:
CRITERION: Earned idea payoff from the premise
DESCRIPTION: Score 5 when the story works out a genuine implication of its own premise that the reader was not handed -- a mechanism, a paradox, a social logic, an inverted consequence -- and the working-out is legible in the text. Score 1 when the premise is illustrated but never interrogated, so the story ends knowing exactly what it knew at the start.

name: Controlled pacing

CRITERION: Controlled pacing
DESCRIPTION: The allocation of narrative time fits the importance and emotional weight of events, without a sagging middle, needless rush, or disproportionate digression.
GUIDANCE: Judge variation and control, not simple speed. A slow passage can score highly when its duration is purposeful.

CRITERION: Diction precision and internal consistency
DESCRIPTION: Judge whether word choices are used correctly and consistently, and whether small factual/continuity details (spelling of body parts, repeated invented terms) are handled with control, distinguishing genuine precision from small slips a careful editor would flag. name: One-line beats that earn their isolation
frozen_block:
CRITERION: One-line beats that earn their isolation
DESCRIPTION: This story may set short lines or single sentences off on their own. Judge whether those isolations do dramatic work IN CONTEXT: an isolated line should land a turn, a reveal, a shift of attention, or a beat of silence that the surrounding prose has set up, and the story should return to ordinary paragraphing when nothing is being marked. Score 1.0 when nearly every isolated line is placed where a beat belongs and the effect would be lost if it were folded back into the preceding paragraph. Score 0.5 when some isolations do work and others are arbitrary. Score 0.0 when lines are isolated indiscriminately or habitually, so the breaks mark nothing in particular, AND also 0.0 when the story isolates nothing but plainly needed a beat somewhere. Answer NA only if the story is too short to show any paragraphing pattern. Judge the placement, not the quantity: a story with three well-placed breaks scores higher than one with thirty indiscriminate ones.
